entries.name: Distant Sounds
entries.text: You cup your hand to your ear and make the sign of Ranald’s cross. You can clearly hear a conversation or other noise from anywhere within range — behind a wall, in a distant room, or elsewhere. You must have a specific target in mind and know where they are, such as a person you know is in a certain room or can see through a window. You can also whisper words to the target. Unlike the Cat’s Eyes Miracle, this works with sealed chambers.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Long Reach
entries.text: You weave a riddle saying that which is out of reach is closer than the senses suggest. Your reach is extended by the Range as invisible arms stretch towards whatever is out of your grasp. You can grab or manipulate whatever you reach, take hold of a ladder or ledge, lift an object of 2 Enc or less, and make Sleight of Hand Tests.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Lose the Loot
entries.text: With one hand you touch whatever you have gained illicitly while raising your eyebrows inquisitively towards Ranald. This miracle gives you a strong sense of who and where you can sell your contraband or stolen goods for a decent price. If within a large town or city, you receive an intuition as to where the nearest Fence may be found. How well this Fence regards you is left to the GM, but provided you have no Sin Points they should be at least willing to do business.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Silence Reigns
entries.text: You whisper a rhyme to Ranald and ask him to fool the hearing of others. Anyone within the area of effect hears nothing but normal background noise undisturbed by footsteps, dogs barking, or any other abrupt sound.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Poor Man’s Face
entries.text: You whisper a riddle about riches being in the eye of the beholder. Ranald answers by concealing any valuables on your person. Anyone searching you finds only worthless items — where once there were coins or other precious objects, there are now a few breadcrumbs or a pebble. Ranald keeps your valuables for the duration of the miracle, but beware — for every hour that an object remains hidden in this way there is a 1% chance that he takes a liking to a valuable and keeps it for himself.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Talk Your Way Out
entries.text: You touch your earlobes and silently cross both fingers, hoping Ranald silvers your tongue. This miracle grants you the ability to talk yourself out of even the most compromising situation. You gain a one-off bonus of +8 SL to a Charm Test while you are trying to talk your way out of being caught red-handed.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: The Heat Is Off
entries.text: You pose a question to humanity at large — why don’t they mind their own business? After committing a crime, for the next few hours, people are oddly disinterested in you. The authorities avert their eyes when you pass and others struggle to remember your coming. If using the rules for watch patrols (page 92) subtract three from any score to work out watch presence. If you attempt another crime, the Miracle stops working. All Fellowship-based tests against Fel are at -3 SL as people can’t focus on you or what you’re saying.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Bountiful Fortune
entries.text: You gesture towards several companions with a wave of crossed fingers. For the next Test they take, they can reverse the order of the percentile dice. For example, 82% could become 28%. If this boon isn’t used within Fellowship Bonus Rounds, it is lost.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Crisis of Confidence
entries.text: You whistle a jaunty little tune that throws off the confidence of an opponent. Choose one target in range who is about to take any voluntary Fellowship-based Test. They immediately feel a sense of anxiety about taking the risk and back down, choosing not to try what they had planned. If they must take the test regardless of their choice they suffer a penalty of -20.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Force the Hand of Chance
entries.text: You ask Ranald to instruct the universe to reconsider the odds of a difficult challenge. This miracle improves your chance of passing a specific Test by +1 SL, but you can increase the advantage by an additional SL if you roll 1d10 and score 6 or less. You can keep making this roll and increase your score by +1 SL as long as subsequent rolls are successful. However, should you score a 7 or more, you lose all accrued bonus SL and must take the original Test at -1 SL.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Perfect Empathy
entries.text: Like a cat sneaking silently into the shadows, you slip into someone else’s mind. You perfectly understand someone to whom you are speaking — regardless of language, you know their meaning, their intentions and what’s on their mind. How you use this information is up to you.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: The Gamemaster
entries.text: You invoke Ranald as master of all games and request that he shares his wisdom with you. When observing any game, sport, or similar leisure pursuit, you are instantly aware of the rules and best strategies to win. If the game involves mental skill (rather than pure chance, physical prowess), all Tests you take to compete in the game are taken at +4 SL. When the effects of the Miracle wear off, you forget everything but the rules.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Up the Stakes
entries.text: You pray quietly to Ranald to exaggerate the effects of your luck. This miracle improves the consequences of success or failure. Take any Test as normal: if you succeed, the result is automatically an Astounding Success. If you lose, it’s an Impressive Failure.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: A Suitable Sucker
entries.text: When finding a mark you pray to Ranald to direct you to the perfect patsy to exploit. Whilst the miracle is in effect the Character may reroll any results on the Contents of a Purse Table (page 28) and the Victim Quirk Table (page 29). If they choose to reroll the second result stands.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Bamboozle
entries.text: You pose a quandary about the nature of free will in a universe ruled by gods. You fool one Human-sized creature into doing your bidding unless it can pass a Hard (−2 SL) Cool Test. You can determine what it does the following round, providing it doesn’t directly harm itself — indirectly is another matter. Creatures with the Undead or Daemonic Traits cannot be bamboozled.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364). Ordinary printed numerical bonuses remain unchanged.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: One Almighty Lie
entries.text: You take a deep breath, cross both fingers and tell the most outrageous lie you can imagine. This miracle allows you to convince people of a falsehood so colossal surely nobody would make it up. Roleplay the lie, then take the Pray Test to invoke the Miracle. If you pass, roll a d10 and add the SLs from the Pray Test. This total is the number of +SLs to add to your Charm Test. The GM may want to reward you with additional SLs if your lie is particularly entertaining (but not plausible!)
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Ranald’s Mischief
entries.text: You mock and mimic an adversary to even up an unequal contest. This miracle allows you to temporarily change two Characteristics to be the same as an opponent for the purpose of an Opposed Test with that opponent. Roll twice to see which are affected (re-roll duplicate results): Characteristic table (p. 24): d10 1–2 Weapon Skill; 3–4 Intelligence; 5–6 Fellowship; 7–8 Initiative; 9–0 choose any Characteristic. Roll twice, rerolling duplicates.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Unremembered Face
entries.text: You whisper a quick prayer to Ranald and ask him to cloud the memories of those you meet. Any creature you meet must pass a Hard (−2 SL) Cool Test to remember more than two facts about your appearance. You choose what they remember, so many priests of Ranald wear distinctive items of clothing which can quickly be removed or hidden.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364). Ordinary printed numerical bonuses remain unchanged.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Back At You
entries.text: You hold out the palm of your hand with fingers crossed. This miracle is directed at any combat within range other than one you are engaged in yourself. Determine the weaker participant by comparing S, T, and WS — whoever is higher in 2 or more Characteristics is strongest. Whilst this miracle is in effect, any Wounds inflicted by the strongest participant during a single attack may be added to the Wounds inflicted the next time the weaker participant causes Damage to the strongest participant.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Class War
entries.text: You call Ranald’s attention to the inequity of society and he responds by cursing the privileged. This miracle requires a Gold Tier target. They are afflicted by a curse identical to the effects of Curse of Ill-Fortune (Fourth Edition WFRP Core Rulebook, page 255). It lasts a day for every level of Gold Standing they have, plus one day per +SL from the Pray Test. If the target habitually follows Ranald’s strictures the curse has no effect.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Free Your Mind
entries.text: You implore Ranald for the strength to resist the commands of authority. This miracle allows you or a chosen target to automatically resist the effects of any Charm or Leadership Test made by a Character with a higher status than the target, no matter how compelling.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Moment of Clarity
entries.text: You intone a riddle about the purpose of existence and Ranald answers with a spiritual wink. For a brief instant you see with total clarity the absolute absurdity of life and everything mortals do. Nothing really matters… and that’s hilarious. For the duration of this miracle you have the Immunity to Psychology Trait.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Rally Round
entries.text: You sing a loud song of Ranald, and the crowd join in. This miracle affects all allies within the area of effect and becomes more effective with numbers. Allies gain +2 SLs to Endurance and Cool Tests, increasing by an additional +SL for every 10 people in the crowd. This Miracle does not affect characters of Silver or Gold Status.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Under my Protection
entries.text: You call Ranald’s attention to the cruelty of the powerful. This miracle requires a target who has threatened or persecuted a victim of your choice — a bullying noble, a racketeer, a prejudiced priest, or similar example of an unjust authority figure. From their next sleep onwards, Ranald inflicts terrifying dreams on them, in which the victims take revenge, they are chased by a giant black cat, magpies pull them apart, and similar nightmares. Whilst suffering such dreams, the target must take a Challenging (+0 SL) Cool Test each morning. If they fail they suffer from a Fatigued Condition. If they treat their victims with kindness or otherwise make amends, the dreams end.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364). Ordinary printed numerical bonuses remain unchanged.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Auroch’s Heart
entries.text: You pray to Taal to suffuse a character with the constitution of a wild oxen. The target gains +Fellowship Bonus SL to all Toughness Tests until the end of the miracle.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Earthshudder
entries.text: You cry Taal’s name three times and cast your arms to the heavens in supplication. In return, the Lord of the Wild sends thunder and shakes the earth. All targets within Fellowship Bonus yards of a target point must pass a Difficult (−1 SL) Athletics Test or gain the Prone condition. Artificial structures (i.e. built rather than natural) within the area of effect sustain d10 +SL damage.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364). Ordinary printed numerical bonuses remain unchanged.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Nature’s Repast
entries.text: You reach out and intone an invocation to Taal, thanking him for his generosity of gifts from the land. This miracle requires food foraged or hunted from the wild. When touched, it becomes more sustaining and nutritious, filling bellies far better than it would have in its original state. Anyone eating the food can go four days without an Endurance Test for starvation. This miracle can affect up to six individual meals and it does not increase the amount of food — so it doesn’t feed more mouths, rather the food itself becomes more sustaining.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Pax of Taal
entries.text: You whisper a guttural, animalistic prayer to Taal. As the words leave your mouth, all beasts in the area of effect fix their eyes on you. All natural animals (with Int 25 or lower) within the area of effect become calm. They will not attack any targets, including prey or one another. This miracle does not work on bipedal creatures or those twisted by Chaos. If anyone attacks the animals, the effect on them is broken.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Rending Paw
entries.text: You roar out a challenge with the ferocity of the Lord of the Wild at his most enraged. He grants you or an ally with a surprising strength of arms. The target gains +20 to their Strength characteristic until the end of the miracle.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: River’s Blessing
entries.text: You implore Taal as Lord of Rivers to grant you safe passage through his domain. For the duration of the miracle you gain +4 SL to all Swim Tests and your speed is your Movement rate when moving through water, rather than half. Note — this miracle has no effect in salt water.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Wild Wind
entries.text: You call to the Lord of the Wild and in response he whips up the wind into a raging, swirling maelstrom. While you are not affected, all targets within the area of effect are buffeted by irresistible winds. Any Test they take against WS or Agi is reduced by -2SL and each round they must pass a Difficult (−1 SL) Toughness Test to avoid a Prone condition. No ranged attacks can be used within the area of effect, and only gunpowder or artillery weapons can attack targets within the area of effect.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364). Ordinary printed numerical bonuses remain unchanged.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Wilderness Way
entries.text: You close your eyes and make the stag sign of Taal with your left hand, waiting for the Lord of the Wild to guide your feet. This miracle can be performed before the party undertake a period of travel as described in Chapter 7 -Pathfinding (page 112). Record the number of SL scored on the Pray Test. These can be used to reroll the results of any Planning Endeavour, Travel Endeavour, or Camp Endeavour made in the following period of journey time. If the journey is interrupted by an encounter the remaining rerolls are lost, though the miracle can be attempted again before the next stage of the journey commences.
entries.conversion: Miracle effects remain reference text. No temporary Characteristic changes, Conditions, command Tests, travel rerolls or campaign actions are applied to the created character.

entries.name: Bag of Tarrabeth Seed
entries.text: Whilst Tarrabeth is a healing herb its seed is pungent and sweet, and is used in cooking. Some dogs find the scent stimulating and distracting, so burglars occasionally use it to distract guard dogs. If a Character is being tracked by dogs, they may leave a bag of Tarrabeth seed in their path. Dogs who come within 5 yards of the bag should make an Average (+2 SL) Willpower Test. Those who fail the Test spend D10 rounds investigating the bag before taking up the trail again. If a dog scores an Astounding Failure (-6 SL or less), they are so distracted by the scent that they forget about the original trail they were following.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 32. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364).

entries.name: Bag of Soot
entries.text: The finest soot is said to come from the cannon foundries of Nuln. A Character can use a bag of soot to stain their clothes, equipment, and exposed skin, making surfaces dark and dull. A character who is covered in soot is harder to perceive in the dark. Any Characters suffer -1 SL to sight-based Perception Tests made to spot the Character or discern anything about their appearance.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 32. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.

entries.name: Caltrops (12)
entries.text: These many-sided spikes are sometimes scattered on battlefields to make areas unsafe for cavalry. A Character with caltrops may use an Action to scatter a dozen of them on the ground, creating a hazardous area 2 yards in diameter. Anyone entering the area must pass a Hard (−2 SL) Athletics Test or be struck by the caltrops. If the Character is aware of the caltrops and moves at walking speed, this Test becomes Average (+2 SL). Characters who fail the Test take a Damage D10 hit to a randomly determined leg and suffer a Surprised Condition.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 32. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.
entries.adaptation: Named Fourth Edition Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I p. 364).

entries.name: Crampons (2)
entries.text: Crampons are wooden frames fitted to boots. Horseshoe nails are hammered through the frame to assist in scaling steep surfaces. Whilst wearing a pair of crampons, Tests made by a Character have the following modifiers: 0 +2 SL to Climb Tests made to scale a rocky or wooden surface 0 +1 SL to Climb Tests made to scale a rope 0 -1 SL to Athletics or Agility Tests made outside the context of climbing 0 -2 SL to Stealth Tests made outside the context of climbing 0 -2 SL to any other Test involving movement made outside the context of climbing (it is best to remove crampons before attempting your dance steps)
entries.conversion: Description: p. 32. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.

entries.name: Glass Cutter
entries.text: A short metal rod tipped with a hard shard of diamond or Stonehorn. A Character equipped with a glass cutter can use it to bore a hole through a pane of glass or scratch out a panel that may then be knocked in with a mallet. Doing this requires an Average (+2 SL) Art (Engraving) Test. Glass Cutting Success Table (p. 33): +1 or more, cut a hole/panel without complication; +0, cut it but with normal breaking-glass noise; −0, bore the hole and take a Damage 3 hit to the primary hand; −1 or less, the window shatters noisily and the primary hand takes a Damage 3 hit.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 33. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.

entries.name: Periscope
entries.text: Pioneered by Dwarf Engineers for the purposes of providing a view to the crews of their submersible ships, a periscope is a device employing mirrors to allow Characters to peep around corners or over objects without exposing themselves. A simple periscope may be nothing more than a mirror lashed to the short rod, but purpose- built devices that house two angled mirrors within a sturdy frame are available. A Character with a periscope may use it to make sight-based Perception Tests while keeping their body hidden or within cover.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 33. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.

entries.name: Smoke Bomb
entries.text: A typical smoke bomb consists of a metal or ceramic vessel containing an alchemical cocktail, which is wadded in and lit by a fuse. A smoke bomb can be thrown exactly like an incendiary, though it does not burn at such a high temperature. Instead, it produces a thick cloud of smoke. The smoke is thick enough to fill a large room or an area 10 yards in diameter in the open air. The cloud persists for 2D10 Rounds (double the number if the bomb is employed in an enclosed space). Characters may not see through the smoke cloud and may only see 1 yard if within the smoke cloud. Furthermore, the smoke is not breathable, and any Character caught in the cloud must test to see if they suffer from Suffocation as described on page 181 of the Fourth Edition Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay Core Rulebook. Smoke bombs are, therefore, effective ways to clear a room or cover an escape.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 33. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion.

entries.name: Thin Jimmy
entries.text: Named for one of the legendary companions of Ranald, this is a small thin steel tool that can be slipped between a door and the jamb in the hope of levering a bolt aside. Whilst a crowbar is used to lever a door open despite a lock, and a lockpick is used to spring a lock open, a Steel Mummit acts on the bolt in the hope of jiggling it loose without the need to operate any mechanism. If a door is locked with a lock and key (not a padlock), or if it is bolted shut, a Steel Mummit may be used to open it if a Character passes a Hard (−2 SL) Sleight of Hand Test. Steel Mummit Success Table (p. 33): +1 or more, open the lock/bolt undamaged and it can be relocked; +0, open it but ruin the mechanism/bolt, visibly needing repair; −0, fail to open it; −1 or less, fail and make loud scraping audible in adjoining rooms.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 33. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion. User-approved printed naming mismatch: table Thin Jimmy uses the description headed Steel Mummit. The naming correction alone is not a Legacy adaptation.

entries.name: Telescopic Pole
entries.text: This stick has the appearance of a walking cane with a hooked handle. In fact, it may be extended into a pole of twelve feet in length. The pole may be used to manipulate objects at a distance, such as unlatching windows on an upper floor or reaching through prison bars to a set of keys. A Character may make Dexterity Tests using the telescopic stick to manipulate objects up to 4 yards away. The pole is unwieldy, so any Tests made whilst using it suffer from -2 SL.
entries.conversion: Description: p. 33. The p. 32 prices and Availability are a rough guide for discreet artisan-made tools; ordinary market purchases may arouse suspicion. Their appearance varies widely, but most combine human and bestial features, often with the head and legs of a goat and the torso and arms of a man. All gors possess a large pair of horns, the defining mark that distinguishes them from ungors and turnskins. Among beastmen, larger horns command greater status, and the biggest gors are known as bestigors.

sections.Traits: Champion: If the creature wins an Opposed Test when defending in melee combat, they can cause Damage as if they were the attacker Corruption (Moderate): Is a Corrupting Influence with a Strength of Moderate Daemonic 8+: Not reliant on air, food, water, and other things needed to sustain life. Roll 1d10 after any blow is received: if the creature rolls 8 or higher, the blow is ignored, even if it is a Critical. They may not use this ability to ignore Magical blows. If reduced to 0 Wounds, the creature is removed from play. Dark Vision: See in the dark as daylight Fear: The creature causes Fear, see page 183 for details Frenzy: Test WP to enter Frenzy: Free Attack each Round, +1 Damage, may only attack or move to attack Hatred (Daemons of Slaanesh): Must attack by fastest and most deadly means possible, +1 SL on Melee and Ranged Tests, immune to Intimidate and Fear caused by them Mark of Chaos (Khorne): See page 359 for details Painless: All non-amputation penalties suffered from Critical Wounds are ignored Unstable: If the creature ends a Round Engaged with opponents who possess Advantage when they do not, they are driven back, and they lose 2 Wounds BloodleTTer of khorne Khorne’s chosen, bloodletters stalk the battlefields of the Old World, harvesting skulls in honour of the Blood God. Needle- like teeth jut from their monstrous, horned visages, and their blood-red skin is covered in scales as hard as brass. Each bears a Hellblade, a wickedly sharp weapon steeped in gore, wielded with the savage fury for which Khorne’s daemons are feared. Daemons cannot manifest for long, because the material world itself rejects them. The havoc they wreak before being banished is so profound, however, that none who encounter a daemon ever forget the mind-fracturing experience.

Skills: Channelling (Any) +10, Cool +10, Dodge +10, Intuition +10, Language (Magick) +15, Melee (Basic) or Melee (Polearm) +10, Perception +10. Talents: Aethyric Attunement or Instinctive Diction, Arcane Magic (Any) or Chaos Magic (Any), Petty Magic, Second Sight. Recalculate Wounds. Choose up to 3 Petty spells and up to 3 spells from a suitable Lore.

entries.name: Spellcaster Lord
entries.text: Characteristic adjustments: WS +10, I +20, Ag +15, Int +20, WP +20, Fel +10. Skills: Channelling (Any) +20, Cool +20, Dodge +20, Intuition +20, Language (Magick) +20, Leadership +10, Melee (Basic) or Melee (Polearm) +10, Perception +20. Talents: Aethyric Attunement, Arcane Magic (Any) or Chaos Magic (Any), Instinctive Diction 2, Luck, Magical Sense, Menacing, Petty Magic, Second Sight, Sixth Sense. Recalculate Wounds. Choose up to 6 Petty spells and up to 9 spells from a suitable Lore.

rows.name: Climb
textFields: The ability to ascend steep or vertical surfaces, like a perilous mountainside or the rain-slick wall of a tumbledown townhouse. Climbing can sometimes be used in combat when facing especially monstrous foes — see page 162 for combat movement.

rows.name: Consume Alcohol
textFields: How well you can handle alcohol without letting it cloud your judgment or render you senseless. Often used to impress those who find the ability to down an unreasonable number of beverages to be praiseworthy.

rows.name: Cool
textFields: Allows you to remain calm under stress, resist fear in the face of horror, and stick to your convictions. It is generally used to resist the attempts of others to Charm or Intimidate you, or to curtail other Psychological effects (see page 183).

rows.name: Dodge
textFields: Avoid things through ducking, diving, and moving quickly, and is used extensively to sidestep falling rocks, incoming weapons, and the like. In combat, Dodge is generally used to resist attacks or avoid damage.

rows.name: Drive
textFields: Maneuvering vehicles — most commonly simple carts and lumbering coaches, but also the more experimental creations of Imperial Engineers — along the roads of the Empire with as little incident as possible.

rows.name: Endurance
textFields: Called upon when you must endure hardship, withstand deprivation, stand without moving for long periods of time, or survive harsh environments. In particular, Endurance is Tested to resist or recover from various Conditions (see page 184) and helps you recover lost Wounds (see page 170).

rows.name: Entertain
textFields: Specialisations: Acting, Comedy, Singing, Storytelling. Delight crowds with the spoken word, perhaps by singing, acting, or attempting a few jokes — hopefully entertaining all those within earshot.

rows.name: Evaluate
textFields: Lets you determine the value of goods. Everybody is assumed to know the relative worth of general items, but Evaluate allows you to identify the value of curious and unique items, recognise forgeries, or spot flaws.

rows.name: Animal Care
textFields: Care for animals and heal them from disease or injury. A Character with an Advance in this Skill can keep animals healthy under normal conditions without needing to Test. A Test is required to diagnose or resolve problems with animals, such as spotting signs of illness or healing an injury (page 171).

rows.name: Athletics
textFields: Your ability to run, jump, move or perform any other general physical activity.

rows.name: Bribery
textFields: Find someone who is willing to accept a bribe, such as a guild notary to accept forged paperwork or a gate guard to look the other way while you slip inside after nightfall. You can also make a Bribery Test to judge if a particular person could be bribed, and what their price is likely to be.

rows.name: Charm
textFields: Makes people think favourably of you, your opinions, and actions you propose. People won’t necessarily do what you say simply because you’ve passed a Charm Test, but they will at least give you due consideration.

rows.name: Charm Animal
textFields: Your aptitude for befriending, quickly calming, or subjugating animals. A Charm Animal Test can convince a wild animal to back off, or a guard dog to devour a proffered scrap of meat rather than your arm.

rows.name: Intuition
textFields: Gives you a feel for your surroundings, to notice when something is wrong, and read people to sense when they are lying or hiding something.

rows.name: Language
textFields: Specialisations: Bretonnian, Reikspiel, Wastelander, and many more. See page 149. Access to extra languages beyond your native tongue. A single Advance is enough to make yourself understood in that language, but a Test may be required to comprehend complicated discussions. Once you have 4 Advances, you count as fluent and no longer need to make Tests.
Albion Battle Bretonnian Classical Elthárin Estalian Gospodarinyi Grumbarth Guilder Haffennaff Khazalid Magick Norse Pilgrim Sign Queekish Reikspiel Thieves Tongue Tilean Wastelander

rows.name: Leadership
textFields: Your ability to lead others and command respect. While most often associated with martial situations, a resolute leader can quickly direct a fast response to a fire or other such calamity, and nobles use the Skill frequently to command their lessers.

rows.name: Lore
textFields: Specialisations: Engineering, Geology, Heraldry, History, Law, Local*, Magic, Metallurgy, Science, Theology. Knowledge of a subject you have been taught or have first-hand knowledge of. Basic facts related to a specific Lore Skill can be recalled easily, with a Test required only to recall obscure or unusual information.

rows.name: Navigation
textFields: Allows you to find your way in the wilderness, or across the ocean, using landmarks, stellar bodies, charts, or maps.

rows.name: Outdoor Survival
textFields: Used to survive in the wild, including the ability to fish, hunt, forage, and build fires and shelters. Experienced survivors are practiced at reading the signs of incoming inclement weather, making do with minimal tools, and noticing the spoor of local beasts.

rows.name: Gamble
textFields: Measure the likelihood that a bet will pay off, as well as successfully engage in various games of chance. If you wish to improve your chances through cheating, see page 135.

rows.name: Gossip
textFields: Ferret out interesting and useful news, and spread rumours of your own. Best practised at a town square, inn, well, or other gathering place.

rows.name: Haggle
textFields: Secure better deals when negotiating with others, when purchasing goods for example. Typically involves an Opposed Haggle Test (page 131).

rows.name: Heal
textFields: You have been trained to deal with injuries and diseases. A successful Heal Test allows you to diagnose illness, treat a disease, heal wounds or staunch a Bleeding Condition. Full rules for illness, injury, and treatments can be found on page 172.

rows.name: Intimidate
textFields: Coerce or frighten sentient creatures — generally with an overt threat, though sometimes a subtle implication or even a look is enough.

rows.name: Pray
textFields: Invoke, appeal to, or otherwise commune with a deity. For more information on using the Pray Skill to seek divine intervention, see Chapter 7: Religion and Belief.

rows.name: Ranged
textFields: Specialisations: Blackpowder, Bow, Crossbow, Engineering, Entangling, Explosives, Sling, Throwing. Anyone can throw a rock, but it takes training and practice to use weapons like bows, pistols, and throwing knives. Each Ranged Specialisation is specific to a group of ranged weapons. If you do not have the Ranged Specialisation for a weapon you wish to use, refer to Chapter 11: Consumer Guide for the penalties you will suffer when using the weapon.

textFields: Your prowess at pulling an oar to move a boat through the water. A Row Test is typically only needed when racing, navigating rapids, desperately avoiding bog octopuses, or similar challenging feats.

rows.name: Sail
textFields: Operate and manoeuvre a sailing vessel — including knotwork, steering, gauging the wind, and more. Sail is required to operate your own vessel, either alone or as part of a crew. If you are commanding a well trained crew, use Leadership instead.

rows.name: Perception
textFields: Your ability to notice things with your senses — sight, smell, hearing, touch, taste, and any other senses you may possess, such as magical or inhuman senses.

rows.name: Perform
textFields: Specialisations: Acrobatics, Clowning, Dancing, Firebreathing, Juggling, Miming, Rope Walking. You have learned a physically demanding art, perhaps as a way to make a living. A successful Perform Test lets you entertain those near enough to see you.
Acrobatics Clowning Dancing Fight Firebreathing Juggling Miming Rope Walking

rows.name: Pick Lock
textFields: You know the mechanisms of locks and how to open them without their proper keys. Many locks are simple affairs made to vex only untutored thieves, while others can be complex dwarf-made mechanisms capable of frustrating all but the most determined plunderer.

textFields: Specialisations: Grey Order, Guild (Any One), Ranger, Scout, Thief, Vagabond. You have been taught how to use clandestine markings only intelligible to members of a select group. Vagabonds might indicate which homeowners are likely to offer alms, thieves may want to indicate territorial markings or warnings, while scouts may want to warn one another about a dangerous monster’s lair nearby (see page 138).

rows.name: Set Trap
textFields: From a simple snare or bear trap, to more spectacular devices like Von Grizzel’s Thief-render, players are unlikely to venture far in the Old World without encountering traps. The Set Trap Skill measures your ability to set and disarm traps of all varieties.

rows.name: Sleight of Hand
textFields: Your ability to pick pockets, palm objects, and perform minor tricks of prestidigitation, as well as cheat at games of chance. This Skill is typically Opposed by the Perception Skill of your target.

rows.name: Stealth
textFields: Specialisations: Rural, Underground, Urban. Move and hide without being detected, blend into a crowd, or otherwise avoid drawing attention to yourself.

rows.name: Stealth (Rural)
textFields: Specialisations: Rural, Underground, Urban. Move and hide without being detected, blend into a crowd, or otherwise avoid drawing attention to yourself.

rows.name: Stealth (Underground)
textFields: Specialisations: Rural, Underground, Urban. Move and hide without being detected, blend into a crowd, or otherwise avoid drawing attention to yourself.

rows.name: Stealth (Urban)
textFields: Specialisations: Rural, Underground, Urban. Move and hide without being detected, blend into a crowd, or otherwise avoid drawing attention to yourself.

rows.name: Swim
textFields: Moving and staying afloat in water. If you have the Swim Skill, you are automatically presumed to be able to swim freely without a Test. But if you find yourself in difficult currents, racing, or fleeing from a ravenous stirpike, a Test will be required.

rows.name: Track
textFields: Your ability to follow subtle trails left by others. Track is used to follow and find your target, as well as to hide your trail.
