rows.name: Conjuration of the Incarnate Elemental of Death
textFields: CN: 90 Type: Lore of Death Learning XP: 500 Ingredients: An hourglass filled with sand made from the powdered bones of a monarch (this Ingredient is not consumed as such, but does become an integal part of the Elemental). Conditions: Extreme Saturation, an Arcane Fulcrum, or a Storm of Magic (see Chapter 14). Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test or gain a Fatigued Condition. Consequences: Individuals within Willpower Bonus yards of the spellcaster, including the caster, suffer Damage equal to the caster’s Willpower Bonus and suffer the Prone Condition. This is a magical attack that is not reduced by Toughness Bonus or Armour Points. The twin-headed serpentine form of an Incarnate Elemental of Death (page 175) hatches from the hourglass.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Conjuration of Jack o’ Cinders
textFields: CN: 85 Type: Lore of Fire Learning XP: 500 Ingredients: A colossal pyre must be constructed and kept ablaze whilst the ritual is in progress. Conditions: Extreme Saturation, an Arcane Fulcrum, or a Storm of Magic (see Chapter 14). Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or gain a Fatigued Condition. Consequences: Individuals within Willpower Bonus yards of the spellcaster, including the caster, suffer 4 Ablaze Conditions. From the inferno you summon forth an Incarnate Elemental of Fire (page 174).
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Corrupt Waystone
textFields: CN: 60 Type: Any Dark Lore Learning XP: 450 Ingredients: None. Conditions: Other than needing access to a waystone no conditions are necessary. Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or gain a Fatigued Condition. Consequences: The ritual fails. You alter the properties of a waystone, corrupting it to produce the effects described on page 194. If the waystone is part of a planned leyline, not only does this affect the stone in question, but magic stops flowing through the leyline. Magic coalesces and stagnates around the closest ‘upstream’ waystone that isn’t also corrupted. The next stone in line becomes a new gathering stone, and then magic is passed on from this point. This corruption is quickly noticed by the High Elf Mages of Saphery, who will make it a priority to locate the source of the disruption and hunt down those responsible.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Create Construct
textFields: CN: 60 Type: Any Lore Learning XP: 400 Ingredients: A suitable form for the construct to inhabit. Conditions: No conditions necessary. Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or permanently lose a point of either Strength or Toughness. Consequences: The ritual fails. You create a magical Construct from the supplied body. Its default profile and optional Creature Traits are on p. 30.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Create Familiar
textFields: CN: 45 Type: Any Lore Learning XP: 250 Ingredients: You must prepare a suitable vessel for the familiar. This could be almost anything from a marionette to a pet cat, a small skeleton, or a grimoire. More information on vessels is found on page 180. An idea or concept may serve as a vessel, but double the CN if so. Conditions: No conditions necessary. Sacrifices: Familiars are a serious investment. The spellcaster must permanently surrender either a Wound, a Fate point, or a point of maximum Fortune during the ritual. Consequences: The ritual fails and the vessel is destroyed. You imbue the vessel with a portion of your own essence, as well as a degree of magical power. You now possess a familiar, which can be one of three types: a Power Familiar (which can help with spellcasting), a Spell Familiar (a wizard in its own right), or a Combat Familiar (a magical bodyguard devoted to your safety). Familiars are Characters of their own; they do not necessarily like their creators, but they are bound to protect and obey them. Familiars may even improve over time and even be played by other Players. See page 184 for more information. Most wizards make do with a single familiar, but some create a second. It is a trickier process, as personal essence is used up at a greater rate to imbue an additional familiar with the required potency. The sacrifice is increased to two Wounds, Fate Points, or points of maximum Fortune, and the CN is increased to 80. By default, familiars are assumed to be humanoid in appearance. If a wizard wishes to construct one that deviates from a humanoid appearance, the GM should consider what sort of abilities or deficits result from its new shape. If a wizard seeks to create a more useful servant through altering its form they can do so, though this will make the process of creating the familiar more difficult. The table below indicates how the CN should be altered to account for familiars of greater or lesser complexity. This is not necessarily an exhaustive list but gives GMs some ideas on how creating a familiar may be easier or more complex.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Permanent Resilience expenditure converted to maximum Fortune (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Create Waystone Property
textFields: CN: 40 Type: Any Learning XP: 300 Ingredients: None. Conditions: You must have access to a waystone, which must be an active part of a planned leyline (see page 193). Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or gain a Fatigued Condition. Consequences: The ritual fails. You alter the properties of a functioning waystone to create an Amplification, Containment, Dampening, or Refraction effect. These properties are described beginning on page 194. If the creating the new property disrupts the flow of magic towards the Great Vortex, High Elf Mages from Saphery may, in time, investigate the cause of the magical disruption and mete out harsh consequences to those who caused the interference.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Cursecraft
textFields: CN: 50 (25) Type: Any Lore, though curses are mostly associated with witches. Numbers in brackets represent a reduced difficulty for spellcasters who practise one of the following Lores: Witchcraft, Daemonology, Necromancy, or any Chaos Lore. Learning XP: 200 (100) Ingredients: None, though you require access to the item to be cursed. Conditions: No conditions necessary. Sacrifices: Curses are powered by the lifeblood of the practitioner who creates them. The creator of a curse must sacrifice a single Wound, which will never heal. Additionally, the process is equivalent to Moderate Exposure to Corruption (WFRP, page 182). Consequences: The ritual fails and the ingredients are destroyed. You imbue the item with a magical ability (a boon), that also comes with the deliberate cost of an ironic or dangerous side-effect (a bane). It is up to the player and GM to decide on the nature of the benefit and the curse, but several examples of cursed items are provided on page 170.
rows.label: Magic

rows.name: Imbue Staff
textFields: CN: 35 Type: Any Lore of the Eight Winds Learning XP: 100 Ingredients: None, though you will need a quarterstaff or metal rod of similar length, as well as paraphernalia and decorations relating to the caster’s Lore of Magic. Conditions: No conditions necessary. Sacrifices: One Fortune point (the printed alternative is Resolve, which Appendix I converts to Fortune) (these may be regained in due course as usual). Consequences: The ritual fails and the ingredients are destroyed. You imbue the staff with magical symbology and power. It is now an Enchanted Staff (see page 152).
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Resolve expenditure converted to Fortune (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Invocate Daemon
textFields: CN: The Daemon’s Willpower Type: Lore of Daemonology Learning XP: 400 Ingredients: Bounds of good taste inhibit a discussion of ingredients, but Daemons typically pay no heed to mortals unless they know at least one of the names the Daemon uses. The invoker must also cause significant mayhem, suffering, or death during the ritual. Conditions: The invoker must cast Octagram (WFRP, page 256) before beginning the ritual. Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or permanently lose a point of Strength or Toughness (randomly determined). Consequences: The Daemon becomes aware that a mortal has tried to invoke it. Their reaction depends on the Daemon in question, though most find such invasions of their privacy a serious affront. You invocate the Daemon, which manifests inside the Octagram you prepared earlier. It remains there for a number of days equal to the caster’s Intelligence Bonus, after which it returns to the Realms of Chaos. You can communicate with the Daemon during this time, but it is not required to answer you or obey you in any way. Daemonologists must be prepared to make additional sacrifices and bargains once they have invoked a Daemon, but what exactly these bargains are, and what the Daemon is willing to offer in return, is left up to the Player and GM to decide.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Materialise the Living Swamp
textFields: CN: 40 Type: Lore of Death, Lore of Life, Lore of Shadows, Lore of Hedgecraft, Lore of Witchcraft Learning XP: 400 Ingredients: None, though you will need a heartstone (see page 179) and access to a quantity of organic matter. Conditions: Heavy, Extreme, or Corrupted Saturation, an Arcane Fulcrum, or a Storm of Magic. Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or permanently lose a point of Strength or Toughness (randomly determined). Consequences: The ritual fails. Marsh matter and vegetation coalesce into the form of a Fenbeast (see page 179). The creature lives for a number of days equal to your Willpower Bonus. If the Fenbeast enters an area of Extreme Saturation its lifespan is extended whilst it remains there. The creature follows your orders. You can dismiss the Fenbeast at any time, whereupon it collapses into a pile of rotting sludge.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Remove Curse
textFields: CN: 40 Type: Any Lore Learning XP: 200 Ingredients: None, though you require the cursed Item. Conditions: The item must be confirmed as a cursed item through a successful Decipher Curse spell (see page 26). Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test or suffer Moderate Exposure to Corruption (WFRP, page 182). Consequences: The ritual fails. You may opt to lift the curse, removing all boons and banes from the item. A weapon whose curse has been lifted retains its Magical Quality.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: The Crossed Scythes
textFields: CN: Willpower of the entity Type: Lore of Death Learning XP: 400 Ingredients: None, though the caster requires the tools with which to create the carving. Conditions: Before commencing the ritual, the wizard must engrave a symbol of crossed downward-pointing scythes over the entrance to a tomb, cave entrance, gatehouse, or other portal. This requires an Extended Challenging (+0 SL) Art (Engraving) Test to a total of 20 SL. Beyond this portal there must be an Undead creature the Wizard seeks to suppress. Sacrifices: Each Round of Channelling the spellcaster must make an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test or suffer 1 Damage which cannot be reduced by Toughness Bonus or Armour Points. Consequences: The ritual fails; the entity becomes aware of the effort to contain it. Occasionally, an Amethyst Wizard will mark a tomb with a pair of overlaid and reversed Shyish runes. Only a fool would enter such a place, for this symbol warns of great evil slumbering within and acts as a ward against its escape. If an Amethyst Wizard seeks to create such a carving, they must be gifted at channelling Shyish and also deft with a hammer and chisel. Once the symbol is carved and the ritual complete, any Undead creature without the Construct Trait that tries to cross the threshold must make a Very Difficult (–30) Cool Test to do so. If the creature fails the Test, they cannot pass the engraving and must take a Fatigued Condition for every –SL. They must do this even if they would not normally suffer Fatigued Conditions. The creature could try to cross the threshold again the following turn, but would continue to accrue Fatigued Conditions until they pass the Cool Test. The creature can only recover from these Fatigued Conditions after a full night’s rest. Undead creatures with the Construct Trait must make a Very Difficult (-30) Endurance Test. If the creature fails the Test, they cannot pass the engraving and suffer 1 Wound for every –SL.
rows.label: Magic

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Suffuse with Ulgu
textFields: You are suffuse with the Grey Wind of Magic, which those with Second Sight perceive as a shadowy, shifting mist wreathed about your body. You can use your Channelling (Ulgu) Skill in place of the Stealth Skill for all relevant Tests. Further, any successful attempts to cast spells from the Lore of Shadow within 8 yards of you gain +1 SL. This bonus may only be claimed once, no matter how many Characters are Suffuse with Ulgu in a spellcaster’s vicinity.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed limit and effects retained under the approved Fifth Edition adaptation.

rows.name: Bless (Evawn)
textFields: You are watched over by one of the gods and can empower simple prayers. Upon learning the Talent, you manifest all the Blessings of the deity you worship. Under normal circumstances, you may not learn more than one Bless (Deity) Talent. Further, you may not learn the Channelling Skill or the Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic, Magic Resistance, Petty Magic, or Witch! Talents when you have the Bless Talent, and vice versa. You can unlearn this Talent for 100 XP, but will lose all of your Blessings if you do so, and may garner the disfavour of the god you have spurned, with effects determined by your GM.

textFields: Specialisations: Drawing, Engraving, Mosaics, Painting, Sculpture, Tattooing, Weaving, Writing. Create works of art in your chosen medium. The more SL achieved, the better the quality of the final piece. For complicated or large works of art, an Extended Test may be required.
Calligraphy Drawing Engraving Icons Mosaics Painting Sculpture Tattooing Weaving Writing

rows.name: Lore (Runes)
textFields: Runelore covers rune history, materials, identification and effects. The Runesmiths Guild passes it on orally; it cannot be learned from books.

rows.name: Melee (Engineering)
textFields: Specialisations: Basic, Brawling, Cavalry, Fencing, Flail, Parry, Polearm, Two-handed. Training and experience with a single type of close combat weaponry. Each Melee Specialisation indicates expertise in using a specific class of weapon. If you do not have the correct Specialisation for a weapon, you will usually suffer a penalty when using it — see Chapter 11: Consumer Guide for more.
Basic Brawling Cavalry Fencing Flail Parry Polearm Two-handed

rows.name: Secret Signs (Brotherhood of Grimnir)
textFields: Specialisations: Grey Order, Guild (Any One), Ranger, Scout, Thief, Vagabond. You have been taught how to use clandestine markings only intelligible to members of a select group. Vagabonds might indicate which homeowners are likely to offer alms, thieves may want to indicate territorial markings or warnings, while scouts may want to warn one another about a dangerous monster’s lair nearby (see page 138).
Grey Order Guilder Hedgefolk Knightly Order Miner Ranger Scout Smuggler Thief Vagabond

rows.name: Trade (Mason)
textFields: Specialisations: Apothecary, Calligrapher, Chandler, Carpenter, Cook, Embalmer, Engineer, Herbalist, Shipwright, Smith, Tanner. Your ability to practice a trade, to create something or provide a service, as well as your knowledge of the relevant lore surrounding your trade.

Apothecary Art Supplies Barber Boatbuilder Brewer Calligrapher Carpenter Cartographer Chandler Cook Embalmer Engineer Engraver Explosives Farrier Gunsmith Herbalist Poisoner Printing Shipwright Smith Tanner Tinker

textFields: Used to craft, reawaken or deactivate magical runes.

rows.name: Sail (Skycraft)
textFields: Advanced flying-machine operation. Take-off and landing require Average (+2 SL) Tests. Normal Sail does not unlock Skycraft, and Skycraft does not grant normal Sail. Situational operations are references only.

textFields: Specialisations: Engineering, Geology, Heraldry, History, Law, Local*, Magic, Metallurgy, Science, Theology. Knowledge of a subject you have been taught or have first-hand knowledge of. Basic facts related to a specific Lore Skill can be recalled easily, with a Test required only to recall obscure or unusual information.

Art Astrology Beasts Chaos Chemistry Daemons Dragons Dwarfs Engineering Folklore Genealogy Geography Geology Giants Heraldry Herbs History Law Local Magic Medicine Metallurgy Oceans Politics Prophecy Rats Reikland Riverways Routes Science Sigmar Spirits Taxes The Empire Theology Trolls Warfare Witches Wrecks

rows.name: Ancestral Grudge
textFields: There are entries in the Great Book of Grudges — those borne against Orcs, Goblins, and Skaven in particular — that are so grievous they can only be avenged with the extinction of all their kind. You have inherited one of these fabled grudges, and whilst you have no chance of seeing it completed in your lifetime, you are more than happy to do your part. Choose a culture or faction that is the target of your Ancestral Grudge (e.g. Orcs, Goblins, Skaven, Trolls, Daemons of Khorne, etc.). Enter them into your Book of Grudges as the target of your vengeance, per the rules on page 33. You bear this group a Blood Grudge that can never be satisfied. However, every time you win a significant victory against this group — e.g. by destroying their works, taking back something stolen, or killing many of their kind — you gain 50 XP. Each time you purchase this Talent, you gain an Ancestral Grudge against a different faction. At the GM’s discretion, declaring vengeance against a smaller sub-faction can award more XP when you score victory over them — e.g. you gain 75 XP each victory if your target is a specific Goblin tribe, or 100 XP each victory if targeting a specific Human family line.

rows.name: Bludgeoner
textFields: You smash more powerful enemies into submission with brutal hammer swings to the head, leaving them utterly exposed whilst you finish them off. When you win an opposed Test to activate the Pummel Quality, you inflict an additional Stunned Condition for each level of Bludgeoner.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Crew Commander
textFields: You are practised at managing crews of siege weapons and artillery pieces. As an Action you may make a Challenging (0 SL) Leadership Test to help a crew manning a weapon with the Crewed Flaw within earshot. If you succeed, the crew members may use your Ranged Skill on the next attack using the weapon.

rows.name: Demolisher
textFields: Cover and armour is no defence against the bite of your axe. When you activate the Hack Quality as part of an attack, you inflict +1 additional Damage on struck armour or shields for each level of Demolisher. In addition, when attacking an enemy in cover with a weapon that has the Hack Quality, hard cover counts as medium cover, medium cover counts as soft cover, and soft cover provides no protection at all.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Dragon Belcher
textFields: Certain Goblin tribes have been known to refer to Dwarf firearms as ‘dragon belchers’, for the furious roar and explosion of smoke they discharge as they fire. You make the most of this psychological impact to scatter and pin your opponents with suppressive fire. When you fire a weapon with the Blackpowder Quality, targeted enemies who fail their Cool Test gain an additional Broken Condition for each level of Dragon Belcher.

rows.name: Entrenchment
textFields: You make the most of whatever terrain is available to you to protect yourself and allies from enemy missile fire. When you are in soft cover, attacks against you are Hard (−2 SL) instead of Difficult (−1 SL). When you are in medium cover, attacks against you are Very Hard (−3 SL) instead of Hard (−2 SL).

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I). Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Forgefire
textFields: You are a living battery of runic power, radiating an aura of battle-fury that imbues nearby weapons with the heat of their forging. When you are Engaged, any melee weapons wielded by yourself or an ally within Willpower Bonus yards gain the Penetrating Quality. If an affected weapon is already Penetrating, its attacks now ignore 1 additional point of non-metal armour.

rows.name: Glorious Demise
textFields: Your bloodlust is so strong it overwhelms your body’s natural instinct to rest after trauma. When you gain the Unconscious Condition, you can interrupt the Turn order to make an immediate Melee attack as a Free Action, before you are taken out of action. When you gain the Stunned Condition, you can spend a Fortune point to make an immediate Melee attack as a Free Action. You take your next Turn as usual, which means you cannot take an Action if you’re still Stunned.

rows.name: Harpooner
textFields: As a veteran quareller, you use precision shooting to neutralise your target, impaling them with bolts in extremely painful locations. When you inflict a Critical Hit with a Crossbow weapon, you may increase your roll on the Critical Hit table by +10 for each level of Harpooner, to a maximum of 00. In addition, Crossbow bolts lodged into the target’s body due to the Impale Quality reduce the target’s Movement by 1 per bolt, to a minimum of 1.

rows.name: Kingsguard
textFields: You are sworn to defend the life of your lord, and any they designate under your protection. If that means sacrificing your own life to shield your charge, you are prepared to do so. Any enemy attacks against an ally within 2 yards of you suffers a -10 modifier for each level of Kingsguard. This Talent does not apply to attacks against yourself, nor does it apply if you are currently suffering from a Condition.

rows.name: Liquid Fortification
textFields: Many Dwarfs insist that good ale can steady the nerves and improve the fighting proficiency of a hearty warrior. Nonetheless, a prudent fighter is careful not to become too reliant on alcohol, lest they become afflicted with “brew-fever”. You gain +10 Strength and Toughness after consuming an alcoholic drink. This provides an immediate bonus to your Consume Alcohol Test for consuming the drink, and the benefit continues to apply whether you succeed or fail on that Test. You retain this bonus until an hour has passed since your last alcoholic drink — drinking again can prolong the effect, but does not increase your Characteristic bonuses beyond +10.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Long Memory
textFields: You never forget a face — or a promise. Unlike the Elven Tower of Memories technique (WFRP Core Rulebook), which Dwarfs consider frivolous and flawed, you use a form of sense memory to anchor details in the real places where you witnessed them, by recalling a specific feeling, taste, or smell from that location. When recalling significant events you were involved in previously in the campaign, you can perfectly remember the time, date, location, and visible faces of all individuals present, and exactly what those present pledged to say or do. If recalling a significant event you witnessed before the campaign began, you may need to take an Intelligence Test to remember details, with a difficulty set by the intervening time — Easy (+4 SL) for events mere months ago, Hard (−2 SL) for events a century ago.

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I). Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Magic Defiance
textFields: Core Rulebook) You ground enemy spellcraft through your own body, refusing to be affected by its fickle enchantments. You can Reverse any Test you are obliged to make as part of a magic spell’s effects, as well as Tests to dispel magic with Magic Resistance (WFRP Core Rulebook).

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Master Rune Magic
textFields: You have learned the secret rites of creating a master rune… but whether you have the skill to successfully forge one still awaits to be seen. Choose a master rune from pages 127-131. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a master rune from the specified lists. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen master rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new master rune you can craft. See page 121 for full runesmithing rules. In addition, the first time you acquire this Talent, you also learn all three Doom Runes (page 132).

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Maverick
textFields: You are an experienced, if reckless, flyer, putting your faith in high speed and overwhelming firepower. You do not suffer the -20 penalty on Ranged attacks when using the Flight Creature Trait.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Rune Magic
textFields: You are inducted into the secret arcane traditions of the Dwarfs, with the knowledge of crafting magical runes. Choose a rune from pages 127 -131. You cannot select a master rune. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a rune from the specified lists. Finally, if your Talent specifies a specific rune (e.g. the Rune of Stone), you must choose that specific rune. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new rune you can craft.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Short Fuse
textFields: You time your explosives carefully to detonate at the optimum moment, showering fragments over the widest possible distance. When using an Explosive weapon with the Blast Quality, increase its Rating by +1 for each level of Short Fuse.

rows.name: Tireless
textFields: You endure heavy burdens, tiring journeys, and interrupted sleep with admirable resolve, refusing to let such ordeals dull your mind or slow your fighting strength. When you apply penalties due to suffering from the Fatigued Condition, you may ignore 1 instance of the Fatigued Condition, +1 additional Fatigued Condition for each level of Tireless. For example, a Character with 4 Fatigued Conditions and 2 levels of Tireless would ignore the effect of 3 Fatigued Conditions, suffering only a -10 penalty to all Tests.

rows.name: Underminer
textFields: enemies, but have learned to compensate by attacking from an unexpected angle.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Whirlwind of Death
textFields: You attack in a sweeping, indiscriminate, fury, tearing through whole formations of enemy warriors. As an Action, you can spend 1 Fortune to make a Melee attack against all creatures Engaged with you. The GM chooses one enemy to Oppose this Test. If your attack succeeds, you inflict the same Damage to the same Hit Location against all Engaged creatures, calculated as normal. Do not apply Criticals on Whirlwind of Death attacks, though Critical Wounds are inflicted on enemies reduced to 0 Wounds as normal. You cannot activate any other special attack options as part of a Whirlwind of Death. However, if a Character with Dual Wielder (WFRP Core Rulebook) is wielding two weapons as part of a Whirlwind of Death, they may Reverse their Melee attack Test.

rows.name: Craftsman (Mason)
textFields: You are a true creative talent, sufficiently skilled in a craft to have the potential to elevate it to an art form. Choose a Trade Specialisation. You gain Advantage on Tests of this skill, and may Advance it even if it is not part of your current Career. You may purchase this Talent more than once, choosing a new Trade Specialisation each time you do.

rows.name: Master Tradesman (Mason)
textFields: You are a skilled and reliable artisan. When you take this Talent, choose a Trade Specialisation. When you successfully use this Skill, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die. You may take this Talent more than once, choosing a new Trade Specialisation each time you do.

rows.name: Artistic (Tattoo)
textFields: You have a natural talent for art. You may always advance the Art Skill, even if it is not part of your current Career. When you choose this Talent, pick one form of written or representative art, such as painting or poetry. You gain Advantage on Art Tests when working in that medium. You may purchase this Talent more than once, choosing another art form in which to excel.

rows.name: Savant (Runes)
textFields: You are exceptionally learned and have a significant degree of specialised knowledge in your field of study. Choose any Lore Specialisation you possess. Tests made using this Lore Specialisation are made with Advantage. You may acquire this Talent more than once, choosing a new Lore Specialisation each time you do so.

If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a rune from the specified lists. Finally, if your Talent specifies a specific rune (e.g. the Rune of Stone), you must choose that specific rune. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new rune you can craft.

rows.key: talent:dwarf-guide:talent:master-rune-magic:Master Rune Magic (Weapon: Master Rune of Alaric the Mad)
rows.name: Master Rune Magic (Weapon: Master Rune of Alaric the Mad)
textFields: You have learned the secret rites of creating a master rune… but whether you have the skill to successfully forge one still awaits to be seen. Choose a master rune from pages 127-131. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a master rune from the specified lists. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen master rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new master rune you can craft. See page 121 for full runesmithing rules. In addition, the first time you acquire this Talent, you also learn all three Doom Runes (page 132).

textFields: You are inducted into the secret arcane traditions of the Dwarfs, with the knowledge of crafting magical runes. Choose a rune from pages 127 -131. You cannot select a master rune. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a rune from the specified lists. Finally, if your Talent specifies a specific rune (e.g. the Rune of Stone), you must choose that specific rune. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new rune you can craft.

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.key: talent:dwarf-guide:talent:master-rune-magic:Master Rune Magic (Armour: Master Rune of Adamant)
rows.name: Master Rune Magic (Armour: Master Rune of Adamant)
textFields: You have learned the secret rites of creating a master rune… but whether you have the skill to successfully forge one still awaits to be seen. Choose a master rune from pages 127-131. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a master rune from the specified lists. You can use the Forge Rune Endeavour to inscribe your chosen master rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new master rune you can craft. See page 121 for full runesmithing rules. In addition, the first time you acquire this Talent, you also learn all three Doom Runes (page 132).

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed purchase limit and effects retained, by user-approved adaptation.

rows.name: Rune of Cleaving
textFields: The weapon inflicts +1 Damage for each Rune of Cleaving.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Retribution
textFields: Any Critical Wounds inflicted by this weapon may add +20 to rolls on a Critical Wound table for each Rune of Retribution.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Cutting
textFields: When attacking with this weapon, you may ignore 2 APs of armour per Rune of Cutting on successful hits.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Daunting
textFields: Whilst this weapon is drawn, you gain the Fear Creature Trait (WFRP Core Rulebook). Your Fear Rating is equal to the number of Runes of Daunting. If you already have a Fear Rating, increase by +1 for each Rune of Daunting.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Fire
textFields: Once drawn, the weapon’s blade bursts into flames, providing 20 yards of illumination, and inflicting 1 Ablaze Condition on enemies it inflicts damage upon. A weapon with two or three Runes of Fire can be used to make ranged attacks using Ballistic Skill, with a Range equal to the wielder’s Willpower Bonus, and the Blast 4 Quality. This attack deals no Damage, but inflicts 1 Ablaze Condition for each Rune of Fire.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Fury
textFields: Whilst wielding this weapon, you gain 1 level of Dual Wielder (WFRP Core Rulebook) for each Rune of Fury, which may exceed the Talent usual maximum levels.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Grudge Rune
textFields: Nominate an enemy you bear a Blood Grudge (page 84). For each Grudge Rune, the weapon gains both +10 to hit and +1 Damage on attacks against the target. At the end of the adventure, if your nominated enemy is slain, you may nominate a new target against whom you bear a Blood Grudge.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Might
textFields: When attacking a target of a larger Size than yourself, the weapon inflicts +3 Damage for each Rune of Might.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Speed
textFields: Whilst carrying this weapon in combat, you gain +10 Initiative for each Rune of Speed.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Striking
textFields: When attacking with this weapon, you gain +10 to your Melee Skill for each Rune of Striking (the specialisation for the Melee Skill being the same as the Weapon Type of the weapon upon which the rune is inscribed). Note that the bonus only applies to strikes with this weapon, so if you are dual wielding with a similar weapon, attacks made with that weapon do not benefit from the bonus.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Alaric the Mad
textFields: Any attacks made by this weapon ignore the target’s AP, the target’s armour Qualities, and any other benefits provided by the target’s armour.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Breaking
textFields: When this weapon makes a successful attack against an enemy who Opposed with Melee, or makes a successful Melee Test to Oppose an incoming attack, any magic weapon used by your opponent during their Melee Test is destroyed.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Flight
textFields: The weapon can be used as a Thrown ranged weapon, with a Range of SB×3. When used on a ranged attack, the weapon gains the Accurate Quality, and returns to your hand after inflicting Damage.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Skalf Blackhammer
textFields: Any successful attack with this weapon counts as scoring a Critical.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of the Slayer
textFields: Choose a specific type of enemy: Daemons, Undead, Dragons, Goblins, Elves, etc. When attacking that target with this weapon, you may Reverse any attack Tests, and Reverse any rolls they make on a Critical Wound table.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Snorri Spangelhelm
textFields: Any failed Melee Tests made with this weapon always count as achieving a success with 0 SL. An attack with this weapon can still fail if the target scores more SLs on their Opposed Test.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Haste
textFields: The weapon gains the Fast Quality (WFRP Core Rulebook), except all Tests to defend against the weapon with Melee suffer a -30 penalty (instead of -10).
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Force
textFields: Whilst wearing this armour, if you make a successful Melee attack as part of a Charge, you inflict bonus Damage for each Rune of Impact equal to the APs of your most armoured location.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Fortitude
textFields: Whilst wearing this armour, you increase your Toughness by +10 for each Rune of Fortitude. Rumours that armour bearing a Rune of Fortitude eventually become sentient are purely speculative.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Iron
textFields: Whilst wearing this armour, you gain +2 Wounds for each Rune of Iron. These Wounds are lost when the armour is removed, which can trigger a Critical Wound for a severely injured Character.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Resistance
textFields: Whilst wearing this armour, you gain +10 for each Rune of Resistance on Tests to Oppose an incoming Melee attack.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Shielding
textFields: Whilst wearing this armour, any incoming ranged attacks or spells reduce the Damage they inflict upon by 2 for each Rune of Shielding. If this reduces Damage inflicted to 0 or less, you do not lose any Wounds.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Stone
textFields: The armour gains +1 AP for each Rune of Stone. Suits with one or more Runes of Stone, and no other runes, are exempt from the Rule of Pride — they continue to function even if identical suits of runic armour enters 100 yards.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Adamant
textFields: When you suffer a Critical Wound whilst wearing this armour, you may Reverse the roll on the Critical Wound table.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Gromril
textFields: The armour loses the Weakpoints Flaw, can never be Damaged except by a Runic Flaw (page 126), and never reduces its AP due to Talents or effects such as the Penetrating Quality. Effects that ignore armour and inflict Wounds directly still apply.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Steel
textFields: Whilst wearing this armour, you can only suffer a maximum of 10 Wounds from any instance when Damage is inflicted.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Clear Sight
textFields: When the talisman is pressed to your eye, you negate any penalties imposed by fog, mist, smoke, or other clouding, non-magical vapours. Two Runes of Clear Seeing also penetrate magical vapours. Two Runes of Clear Seeing allow you to see clearly even in total darkness.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Truth
textFields: The talisman glows brightly if pressed into contact with an item that has been faked, forged, counterfeited, or deliberately degraded in value. Two Runes of Disclosure also identify magical illusions or duplicates. Three Runes of Disclosure reveal the precise method of deception to the bearer.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Far Sight
textFields: When the talisman is pressed to the user’s eye, their vision is magnified, allowing them to clearly see events up to a mile away. Two Runes of Farseeing extend vision up to two miles. Three Runes of Farseeing extend vision up to four miles.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of the Furnace
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, you can never acquire the Ablaze Condition, are immune to heat exposure, and reduce all incoming Damage from fire and flaming attacks by 4 for each Rune of the Furnace.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Luck
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, you gain 1 Fortune point for each Rune of Luck, which can exceed your usual maximum Fortune. You lose these Fortune points when you remove the talisman (to a minimum of 0 Fortune), and cannot regain them until the following session.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Permanent Resilience expenditure converted to maximum Fortune (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Rune of Restoration
textFields: After a good night’s sleep whilst wearing this talisman, the bearer regains their Toughness Bonus in Wounds for each Rune of Restoration.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Spellbreaking
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, and using the Magic Resistance Talent, you can activate a Rune of Spellbreaking to automatically count as rolling 01 on your Willpower Test. You can activate each Rune of Spellbreaking once per adventure, and must choose to activate it before you roll.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Spelleating
textFields: If you successfully dispel a spell using the Magic Resistance Talent whilst wearing this talisman, the spellcaster cannot attempt the spell again for your Willpower Bonus in Rounds. Two Runes of Spelleating extend this effect to your Willpower Bonus in hours. Three Runes of Spelleating extend this effect to your Willpower Bonus in weeks.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Warding
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, you may impose a -10 penalty for each Rune of Warding on attack Tests or spellcasting Tests targeting you.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Balance
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, if an enemy within line of sight casts a spell, you may either Reverse their Spellcasting Test, or Reverse your Opposed Willpower Test (if you’re in range to attempt Magic Resistance).
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Industry
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, you may take an extra Endeavour between adventures.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Kingship
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, you may Reverse any Charm, Intimidate, and Leadership Tests you make that target a Dwarf, or a group mostly consisting of Dwarfs. Rumour has it whoever wears this talisman benefits from the wisdom of the previous bearer.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Passage
textFields: Whilst wearing this talisman, and Moving no faster than walking pace, you can Move through solid, immobile objects like trees, rock, and metal cages. You cannot Move through animals or Undead creatures. You cannot end your Move inside a solid object.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Spite
textFields: Whenever you take Damage from a Melee attack, the attacker immediately suffers 2d10 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points as normal.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Alarm
textFields: The runic item emits a loud, blaring noise if any creature of Size Small or larger enters its range of effect. Two Runes of Alarm may instead bellow a pre-recorded sentence. Three Runes of Alarm may instead transmit a pre-recorded telepathic message to the crafter or their closest living descendant, over any distance.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Battle
textFields: Affected allies begin combat with 1 Momentum for each Rune of Battle.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition Advantage references converted to Momentum (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Rune of Courage
textFields: Affected allies gain +10 on Psychology Tests (WFRP Core Rulebook) for each Rune of Courage.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Discovery
textFields: For each Rune of Discovery the runic item has, the crafter may choose a specific metal or gem (e.g. gold, diamond, gromril, iron ore, obsinite, ithilmar, brightstone). The runic item glows brightly if the specified material appears within its range of effect.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Enemy Detection
textFields: For each rune, describe a type of creature — a general creature type (Skaven, obvious Chaos worshippers), or a more specific description (one-eyed women with red hair). When a creature that clearly matches the description enters the range of effect, the rune glows a violent crimson.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Locking
textFields: Any locks within the runic item’s range of effect are immune to being picked or forced except by magic or the corresponding key. Two Runes of Locking also protect from magical effects. Three Runes of Locking are proof against the lock’s corresponding key — only the crafter, or their closest living descendant, can open the lock at will. A lock may still be bypassed by smashing through the chest or door they protect.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Purification
textFields: Affected allies gain +20 for each Rune of Purification on Tests to resist toxins in air and water.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Retribution
textFields: If a creature violates the sanctity of dead bodies within the runic item’s range of effect (e.g. stealing from the dead, casting a necromantic spell), they immediately gain 1 Ablaze Condition for each Rune of Retribution.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Sanctuary
textFields: Affected allies gain +10 for each Rune of Sanctuary on Willpower Tests to dispel with Magic Resistance.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Slowness
textFields: Enemies attempting to Engage an affected ally reduce the distance they can Run by 4 yards for each Rune of Slowness, to a minimum of the enemy’s Walk distance.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Verminkill
textFields: Rodents, Skaven, and rat-based abominations like Rat Ogres lose 2 Wounds for each Rune of Verminkill (ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points) when they enter the runic item’s range of effect, or start their Turn within it.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Expel Chaos
textFields: Affected allies may Reverse any Test to resist corrupting influences, Tests to avoid mutation from Corruption, and rolls on the Physical and Mental Corruption Tables. In addition, when an affected ally is engaged with a Daemonic enemy that has the Unstable Trait, they count as having +2 Momentum when calculating Wounds lost for being Unstable.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition Advantage references converted to Momentum (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Master Rune of Grimnir
textFields: You may Reverse enemy Ranged attack Tests made against affected allies.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Grungni
textFields: You may Reverse any enemy spellcasting Tests made against affected allies.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Stromni Redbeard
textFields: Affected allies begin combat with 1 Momentum. Double the range of this rune’s effects to 12 yards, or 24 yards if forged upon a battle standard.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition Advantage references converted to Momentum (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Master Rune of Valaya
textFields: Affected allies may Reverse any Willpower Test to Oppose spellcasting with Magic Resistance. The range limit for Magic Resistance is removed — affected allies can Oppose any spell cast against a target in their line of sight — and the Talent can be used to dispel persistent spells (WFRP Core Rulebook), not just incoming spells.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Accuracy
textFields: When attacking with this weapon, you gain +10 to hit for each Rune of Accuracy.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Burning
textFields: A target struck by this weapon gains 1 Ablaze Condition per Rune of Burning.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Forging
textFields: When you Fumble and/or Misfire whilst using this weapon, the crew may activate this rune to negate the effects. You can activate each Rune of Forging once per adventure.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Penetrating
textFields: The weapon inflicts +2 Damage for each Rune of Penetrating.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Reloading
textFields: The weapon reduces its Reload Rating by 2 for each Rune of Reloading. If this would reduce the Rating to 0 or below, the weapon loses the Reload Flaw. Weapons with the Salvo Quality cannot be reduced below Reload Rating 1.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Seeking
textFields: When this weapon attacks a flying enemy, you gain +20 to hit for each Rune of Seeking.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of the Stalwart
textFields: Dwarfs crewing this weapon begin combat with 1 Momentum for each Rune of the Stalwart. This extra Momentum is lost by any Characters that leave the weapon’s crew, or become Engaged in melee.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Fourth Edition Advantage references converted to Momentum (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Rune of the Valiant
textFields: Dwarfs gain +10 Willpower for each Rune of the Valiant whilst crewing this weapon.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Defence
textFields: The weapon’s crew always count as being in hard cover, imposing a -30 modifier on Ranged attacks against them.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Disguise
textFields: The weapon is invisible to all enemies until it fires, at which point it becomes visible for the rest of the combat. The weapon’s crew remain visible as normal, and moving the machine still causes noise.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Immolation
textFields: Any Dwarf crewing this weapon may choose to activate the rune as a Free Action, triggering the machine’s self-destruction. All creatures within 6 yards of the machine take 15 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Survivors gain the Ablaze Condition. The weapon itself is destroyed.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Master Rune of Skewering
textFields: When making a Ranged attack with the weapon, you may activate this rune to count as rolling 01. If the attack succeeds, it also counts as a Critical, and may strike any location you choose. You may activate this rune once per adventure, and must decide to activate it before you roll.
rows.label: Rune

rows.name: Rune of Hearth and Home
textFields: Requires an Anvil of Doom and a Hard (−2 SL) Runesmithing Action (p. 132). The blessing of Valaya affirms a Dwarf’s resolve to fight and die without fear. All Dwarfs within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom may count as rolling 01 on any Cool Tests (WFRP Core Rulebook) they make until the end of the next Round.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Rune of Oath and Steel
textFields: Requires an Anvil of Doom and a Hard (−2 SL) Runesmithing Action (p. 132). The blessing of Grungni enchants the armour of his children with supernatural resilience. All Dwarfs within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom improve the AP of any armour they’re wearing by 2, until the end of the next Round.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Rune of Wrath and Ruin
textFields: Requires an Anvil of Doom and a Hard (−2 SL) Runesmithing Action (p. 132). The blessing of Grimnir unleashes the war god’s fury in a raging storm of splitting earth and darkening skies. All enemies within 25 yards of the Anvil of Doom are struck for 12 Damage to a random location, reduced by Toughness Bonus and Armour Points.
rows.label: Rune

legacy.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

rows.name: Mage
textFields: Student Mage requires four of this guide’s six Petty spells. Additional Colour Lores use 10 individual Channelling points and four qualifying spells, up to WP Bonus; High Magic has the further requirements on pp. 79–83.
